nodes.label: Offline Wheelhouse
nodes.rationale: Empty on purpose; fill it on a connected machine and then the whole project folder is the air-gap bundle. Install with pip --no-index --find-links=wheelhouse.

nodes.label: ARM64 Platform Wheels Required
nodes.rationale: The board is ARM64, so wheels must be downloaded with --platform manylinux2014_aarch64. Wheels built for the laptop's architecture will not install there.

nodes.label: Zephyr UNO Q Board Profile
nodes.rationale: fqbn arduino:zephyr:unoq with the arduino:zephyr platform, pinning SCServo, Ethernet 2.0.2 and Arduino_RouterBridge.

nodes.label: Arduino_RouterBridge
nodes.rationale: Required on the UNO Q for the Linux to MCU Bridge.

nodes.label: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available()
nodes.rationale: accept() hands over a connection exactly once, transferring ownership. available() returns whichever client has unread data and returns that same client again on every call, so an accept loop built on it adopts one connection into several slots and splits one HTTP request across several sockets.
nodes.community_name: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available
nodes.norm_label: adopt connections with accept(), never available()

nodes.label: Detect Disconnects Before Accepting
nodes.rationale: Order inside Poll() matters: disconnect detection, then accept, then pump. If accept runs first a just-dropped slot can be handed to a new connection before net_close is sent, and the Linux side feeds new bytes into the old socket.

nodes.label: Edge-Triggered was_up Disconnect Tracking
nodes.rationale: Act on the was-connected to not-connected transition. Testing !connected() every pass emits net_close continuously for slots that are merely idle.

nodes.label: loop() Must Yield
nodes.rationale: Poll() returns immediately when idle so loop() spins at full speed, starving the Bridge RPC thread until servo_read misses its 10s deadline. A delay(1) at the end of Tick() costs nothing against the latency budget.

nodes.label: One Bulk Read Per Slot Per Pass
nodes.rationale: Use client.read(buffer, sizeof(buffer)), not a byte-at-a-time loop, and never block or delay() inside the pump because the same loop() also drives the servo bus.
nodes.norm_label: one bulk read per slot per pass

nodes.label: kRelayChunkBytes Must Match relay_chunk_bytes
nodes.rationale: One number in two places, bytes per Bridge message. Halving it doubles the number of Bridge round trips for identical payload; 256 is the value the working relay used.

nodes.label: Bridge Net Contract
nodes.rationale: MCU to Linux: net_open(slot, client_ip), net_rx(slot, data), net_close(slot). Linux to MCU: net_tx(slot, data), net_shutdown(slot).

nodes.label: provide_safe Registration
nodes.rationale: net_tx and net_shutdown are called from the Bridge thread while loop() may be inside the relay, so they must be registered with provide_safe. Payloads are MsgPack bin_t and must not be packed into a String.

nodes.label: Serial Works; Monitor Is Optional
nodes.rationale: The sketch prints through Serial and that is proven. Monitor (the Bridge console facade) only adds reach to App Lab over WiFi; there is no correctness reason to switch.

nodes.label: Rewriting Instead Of Porting Reintroduced Solved Bugs
nodes.rationale: The relay was once rewritten from scratch instead of ported, and the rewrite reintroduced problems the original had already solved. The reference is the Stage-2 relay sketch.
nodes.community_name: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available
nodes.norm_label: rewriting instead of porting reintroduced solved bugs

nodes.label: Graphify-first navigation rule
nodes.rationale: A graphify query returns a scoped subgraph at a fraction of the token cost of browsing python/app/ or sketch/src/. Query before grepping; read whole files only to edit or debug specific lines. The rule is explicitly to be propagated into every sub-agent prompt.

nodes.label: One fact lives in exactly one file

nodes.rationale: Without .env, use_hardware_servo defaults to false: the UI moves convincingly while the servo never twitches. Failure is silent, which is what makes it expensive.

nodes.rationale: Read the written reasoning before rewriting; several bugs came from re-deriving solved behaviour. Never bundle unrelated changes. nodes.rationale: A saved, named position an operator captures and can re-select. The genus; the datum is one distinguished member. Avoid preset, bookmark, waypoint, favourite.

nodes.label: Datum
nodes.rationale: The one absolute zero reference, captured by Calibrate from a validated reading at the documented physical reference position. Exactly one, cannot be deleted, must sit mid-travel — a datum at count 0 strands the negative half of the window. Avoid zero point, home, origin, offset.

nodes.label: Baseline
nodes.rationale: The position of the currently active zero reference — the point output degrees are measured from. Activating another zero moves the baseline without disturbing the datum.

nodes.label: Travel window

nodes.rationale: One of six conditions decoded from status register 0x41 (overload, overcurrent, overheat, voltage, sensor, angle). 'Alarm' is the UI's word for a surfaced fault.

nodes.label: timestamp
nodes.rationale: The time field on every entity, schema, DB column, CSV column and query param. Spelled out everywhere — never ts, time or when.

nodes.label: Bridge
nodes.rationale: The RPC channel between the Linux side and the MCU. Calls are serialised; payloads are CSV strings with typed arguments.

nodes.label: Relay
nodes.rationale: The MCU-side byte pump mirroring Ethernet-shield connections to the Linux side. Owns no HTTP knowledge — it moves bytes.

nodes.rationale: CONTEXT.md is a glossary and nothing else. A missing concept is a signal: either invented language, or a real gap worth adding.

nodes.label: Full typing with lowercase builtin generics
nodes.rationale: Every parameter and return typed; list[str]/dict[str,int] rather than typing.List — a deliberate update against the older reference standard.

nodes.label: Optional[X] never X | None
nodes.rationale: Optional is explicit at a glance in a way | None is not; the canonical optional collection is Optional[list[str]].

nodes.label: Google docstrings with types in Args/Returns
nodes.rationale: Args: and Returns: always carry the type in parentheses. Docstrings stay short — a mechanism needing three sentences belongs in a comment at the relevant line.

nodes.label: Class docstrings carry Attributes:
nodes.rationale: Observed in the reference project, absent here: every attribute listed with its type, plus an __init__ docstring with a full Args: block and annotated instance attributes.

nodes.label: Grouped, parenthesised imports
nodes.rationale: stdlib / third-party / local groups; multi-name imports one per line with a trailing comma.

nodes.label: Layout divergence from the reference src/ tree
nodes.rationale: python/app/ instead of src/, routers/ instead of routes/, settings+logging+exceptions folded into core/. Not automatically defects: this is an embedded app, and abstract/+concrete/ expresses the same intent as base_repository.py+mongodb/. Renaming mid-project is churn with no payoff. app.yaml is an Arduino App Lab platform requirement and must not be tidied away.
nodes.community_name: Layout divergence from the reference src/ tree
nodes.norm_label: layout divergence from the reference src/ tree

nodes.label: Trailing commas force vertical layout (ruff)
nodes.rationale: A trailing comma on the last element makes ruff split the collection one item per line — used deliberately. The authoritative ruff config lives on the isolated network and takes precedence.

nodes.label: Three-tier exception hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Exception for abstract levels, Error for concrete: service base (ServoMvpException) -> category (NotFoundException) -> concrete (ServoNotFoundError). Each class carries its FastAPI status code; error codes accumulate with += into SERVO_MVP.NOT_FOUND.SERVO_NOT_FOUND. The payoff is handler count — one handler on the service base reads status, code and metadata off whatever was raised. The repo today has a flat set under DomainError.

nodes.label: Abstract Database with concrete SqliteDatabase
nodes.rationale: The abstract/concrete split applied to repositories should apply to the database itself; the repo has only the concrete Database in python/app/db/database.py.

nodes.label: Control-flow prohibitions
nodes.rationale: Never break, never continue (use an early return), never while True, never list comprehensions — write the explicit for loop.

nodes.label: Explicit boolean checks, no implicit truthiness
nodes.rationale: if value is True / is not None / len(items) == 0; avoid not; parenthesise every term of a multi-term condition.
nodes.norm_label: explicit boolean checks, no implicit truthiness

nodes.label: Naming rules drawn from the glossary
nodes.rationale: No single-letter names; name a variable for what it holds; domain terms come from CONTEXT.md, never a synonym listed under _Avoid_.
nodes.norm_label: naming rules drawn from the glossary

nodes.label: Thin routers, services hold logic, abstract repositories only
nodes.rationale: Routers validate, call a service, return a response — zero business logic. Services take dependencies by constructor injection and depend on repositories/abstract/ only. deps.py is the composition root and the only module naming concrete classes; the simulated/hardware swap happens solely in get_servo_repository().

nodes.norm_label: thin routers, services hold logic, abstract repositories only

nodes.label: C++ sketch-side standard (proposal)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly a proposal, not an existing standard. Carries over full typing, no single-letter names, explicit comparisons and parenthesised terms; adds Doxygen /// on every public method, constexpr over #define, const& for anything larger than a machine word, and every file declaring its own includes because .h files in a sketch are not auto-included.

nodes.label: Drain loops are exempt from the no-while rule
nodes.rationale: RELAY_NOTES.md records that the relay must drain with while, never if, because the 64-byte UART ring overflows at one byte per loop(). The rule is 'no unbounded while (true)', not 'no while'.
